question.text: Mr. Kapoor has invested Rs. 50 lakh in an equity fund and wants regular monthly income. His distributor suggests three options: SWP from Growth plan, IDCW Payout, and IDCW Re-investment. Which option provides the MOST tax-efficient regular income?

answer.text: SWP from the Growth option, as only the capital gains component of each withdrawal is taxed
IDCW Payout, because mutual fund dividends are tax-free
IDCW Re-investment, because the reinvested amount is not taxed
All three options have identical tax treatment

explanation.text: The Logic: An SWP from the Growth option is taxed as a partial redemption — capital gains are booked only when units are sold, so only the capital-gains component of each withdrawal is taxed. The principal-return component is not taxed. IDCW distributions, in contrast, are taxable in the hands of the investor under current laws as per the applicable head/break-up. The Trap: IDCW from mutual funds is not tax-free; both IDCW Payout and IDCW Re-investment are taxable at the time of distribution, and IDCW Re-investment does not escape tax merely because the cash stays inside the fund. Note: Source: NISM Series V-A (Mutual Fund Distributors) workbook, pp.155-167 and pp.202-203 — Growth/SWP capital-gains treatment, IDCW taxability under current laws, and resident IDCW TDS applicable above Rs. 5,000.
